summary: Discovery focused on Southridge Bank's data residency and compliance constraints. Bank favors on-prem/VPC-first approach for PII and regulated workflows; interested in Dedicated with Private control plane for auditability. Key asks: EU/US residency options, KMS/HSM support, SSO + RBAC, ability to restrict or disable request/response logging, long-term audit log retention controls, and SOC 2 / penetration test evidence.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
KMS / HSM / encryption at rest & in transit
Compliance evidence: SOC 2 / ISO / pen tests
Network controls: VPC peering, private endpoints, no public egress
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-08 15:00 ET / Duration ~45 min / Recording: on
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Gupta (Redwood SE), John Reynolds (Southridge Head of IT), Aisha Khan (Compliance), Tom Becker (Cloud Arch), Emily Park (DevOps)

Summary section (auto-gen, may be imperfect): bank asking about data residency, compliance, and options for disabling logs for certain workloads. Some mention of sock two instead of SOC 2 in auto notes.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro from our side, I'm Alex, AE for Redwood. Priya's our SE, Sam's on for any infra deep dives.
[00:12] John (Southridge): Thanks, Alex. We wanted to use this to see where Redwood fits for us. Main things: GDPR applicability for EU accounts, HIPAA for health-related client data, and overall logging / retention controls.
[00:25] Priya (SE): Awesome. High level we support Hosted, Dedicated and Private. Hosted is our managed API, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with isolation, and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane (VPC / on-prem). For banks we usually see Dedicated or Private.
[00:41] Aisha (Compliance): We need to understand where data at rest and in flight live. If we use Hosted, can we guarantee EU only? And what about request/response logs — can they be disabled for certain endpoints?
[00:56] Priya (SE): For Hosted we have region pinning, but for strict residency we recommend Dedicated in a region or Private. Logging: we have configurable retention and the ability to disable storing request/response for regulated routes, though we need to align the SLA and legal. There's a nuance around telemetry vs full transcript storage.
[01:20] Tom (Cloud Arch): When you say 'disable storing', is it per-route? We have internal compliance rules that say no PII leaves the VPC for some workflows.
[01:34] Priya (SE): Yes, per-route and per-env controls are available on Dedicated/Private. For Private you get the strongest guarantee since the control plane can be customer-managed and the data plane can be entirely inside your VPC or on-prem.
[01:50] John: Ok, and KMS? We need HSM-backed keys and audit of key usage.
[01:58] Alex: We integrate with customer KMS — AWS KMS, Google, and also HSM options for Private deployments. Key usage logs are retained and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[02:10] Emily (DevOps): How do you handle SSO & RBAC? We use SAML SSO and need fine-grained roles.
[02:18] Priya: We support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with custom roles; Admin versus dev versus auditor. We can map to your identity provider.
[02:35] Aisha: What about SOC 2 and penetration tests? We need evidence for procurement.
[02:42] Alex: We'll send SOC 2 Type II and ISO reports, plus pen test summary. I will share the security deck after this call.
[02:51] John: Great. Another item: log retention windows. Our risk team wants 7 years for some audit logs. Is that possible?
[02:59] Priya: For audit logs yes, we can configure retention and export to your S3/GCS buckets or SIEM. For request/response transcripts long retention can be sensitive; we can either avoid storing them or store them in your tenant with your retention policy if you're on Dedicated or Private.
[03:18] Tom: If we do Dedicated, do you still have access to request content?
[03:24] Priya: In Dedicated, by default Redwood manages the control plane but you can opt for 'no transcript' mode and push logs to your storage; we can also sign an addendum around access controls. For Private, you control everything.
[03:40] John: What's the typical latency hit for Private vs Dedicated?
[03:46] Sam (Solutions Engineer): Private tends to be similar if deployed in your region; the main differences are networking and initial request routing. We typically see sub-100ms token latency for hosted in region, Dedicated tuned for throughput, Private depends on your infra. There's tradeoffs though — quantization and batching adjustments affect cost/latency.
[04:10] Emily: Speaking of cost, we need numbers. Is there a quick way to model cost for high-volume routing to Dedicated?
[04:18] Alex: We'll provide Dedicated pricing tiers and a sample cost model for your expected throughput. Priya will include suggested batching/quantization profiles to reduce unit cost.
[04:29] Aisha: GDPR question — if a customer in the EU requests erasure, can we remove their prompts from Redwood servers?
[04:36] Priya: If you control the data store (Dedicated or Private) you can delete per your policy. For Hosted we have controls but deletion requests need coordination; that's why many banks prefer Dedicated or Private for strict GDPR controls.
[04:53] John: We also have a regulator that requires proof that data processing for certain models doesn't leave the EEA. How do you handle model variants and fallbacks?
[05:04] Priya: We have routing policies. You can restrict routes to EU-only model variants. If we do cross-region fallback, it's configurable and can be turned off so there's no cross-border processing.
[05:18] Tom: Network-wise, can we do VPC peering or private endpoints? No internet egress from the workload to public endpoints?
[05:25] Sam: Yes, VPC peering, PrivateLink, and private endpoints are supported. For Private deployments, all egress can be controlled by you.
[05:36] Aisha: A couple of items that are important: GLBA is in-scope for us, some PHI workflows too, and we need to know if Redwood accepts BAA for HIPAA workloads.
[05:47] Alex: We do sign BAAs for certain enterprise accounts in Private or Dedicated with controls; we'll include our legal's template for you to review.
[05:58] John: On the logs, our security team mandates immutable audit logs with tamper-evidence. Can Redwood support forwarding signed audit logs?
[06:08] Priya: Yes, we can forward logs to your S3 with object lock or to your ledger, and supply hashing/audit chains. Some of that is easier in Dedicated/Private.
[06:22] John: Great, and pen-test cadence? We need at least annual pen tests and remediation evidence.
[06:28] Alex: We perform annual pen-tests and share summary reports. We can discuss redaction for public-facing components.
[06:38] Aisha: Any limitations on disabling telemetry? We want to keep system metrics for performance but not store prompts.
[06:45] Priya: You can disable prompt storage and still retain telemetry like request rates, latency, token counts. The telemetry is aggregated so it doesn't contain prompt content. Note: some runtime debugging traces may be sensitive; we can route them to your secure logging bucket.
[07:04] Tom: For Dedicated pilot, what infra does Redwood need from our side?
[07:10] Priya: We typically ask for VPC peering, a subnetwork for the Dedicated agents, agreed CIDR ranges, and a bastion for management if Private. We'll provide a checklist.
[07:22] Emily: Does Redwood offer an on-prem package for air-gapped needs?
[07:26] Alex: Yes, Private supports on-prem air-gapped installs; it's heavier operationally but fits regulated workloads.
[07:34] John: Are there references of other banks doing something similar?
[07:38] Alex: We have several; I can share anonymized case studies — e.g., bank X moved high-reg risk workflows to Dedicated with VPC-only egress.
[07:48] Aisha: Competitors often claim 'we don't store data' but then there's hidden telemetry. We need explicit terms in contract.
[07:56] Alex: Totally; we'll surface exact logging/retention terms in the contract and a security addendum.
[08:03] John: On encryption at rest, acceptable algorithms? We use AES-256 and require HSM-backed keys for some workloads.
[08:11] Priya: We support AES-256 and HSM-backed keys via BYOK. Key rotation policies can be set and logs forwarded.
[08:21] Tom: For the pilot, we'd like a 1-week benchmark with real traffic and goal to measure latency, model accuracy drift and cost. Is that doable?
[08:29] Priya: Yes, we can run a pilot in Dedicated; we'll allocate reserved capacity for your workload. We'll need a sample traffic profile and some eval prompts.
[08:40] Emily: Also need to know how model versioning and rollouts are audited — we need traceability when model weights change.
[08:48] Sam: We provide model version metadata, rollout logs, and per-request model id in traces. Those are exportable to your audit log store.
[09:00] Aisha: Quick question, can we anonymize or tokenise PII before sending to Redwood at the SDK level?
[09:07] Priya: Yes, we have SDK hooks and recommend client-side tokenization for extra protection. Many customers use PII tokenization for hosted flows.
[09:18] John: Ok, what's the timeline if we want Dedicated pilot starting mid-December?
[09:24] Alex: We can prioritize it; contract/legal review might take 2-3 weeks. Tech provisioning for Dedicated usually 3-7 days once contracts are signed.
[09:36] Aisha: Our procurement will need estimated costs for dedicated baseline plus burst.
[09:41] Alex: We'll include estimated burst pricing and examples in the pricing deck.
[09:47] Tom: Any restrictions on exporting logs to EU buckets? Some of our auditors want all logs for EU customers to be stored within EEA.
[09:56] Priya: Yes, we can configure region-specific export targets and avoid cross-border replication. It's part of the residency controls.
[10:09] John: A minor thing — sometimes transcripts of calls show 'KV cash' instead of KV cache; just flagging transcription issues for your records.
[10:16] Alex: Ha, noted. Our auto-transcription is imperfect.
[10:20] [10:20-30] brief cross talk, small talk about holiday schedules and availability
[10:31] Priya: I'll prepare the Dedicated vs Private matrix and include a tech checklist for VPC/peering.
[10:38] Alex: I'll send SOC2/ISO and pen test summaries and the contract template addendum for logging and data residency.
[10:45] John: We'll collect the compliance matrix and send to you.
[10:50] Aisha: One last compliance note: we need proof that any sub-processors are vetted and list of subprocessors and their locations.
[10:58] Alex: We'll send the current subprocessor list and locations.
[11:04] Tom: Ok, next steps and owners as a recap?
[11:09] Alex: Recap: Alex send security docs by Fri, Priya send Dedicated pricing and pilot checklist by Sat, Tom provide network diagram mid-next-week, Aisha provide compliance scope list next Tues. Schedule follow-up 2026-12-13.
[11:28] John: That works. Thanks everyone.
[11:32] Alex: Thanks — talk soon.

(End of transcript)
